newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ELECTRICITY FRONT MONTHS EASE WITH CASH.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ELECTRICITY FRONT MONTHS EASE WITH CASH.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Thursday in thin trade in line with cheaper Western physical prices, industry sources said.

As of 1320 EDT, September Palo Verde (PV) was trading down 37 cents at $30.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $30.25-31.00, while October PV was trading up 10 cents at $23.10 per MWh.

September California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 29 cents at the day's high of $23.00 following exchanges as low as $22.55, while October was up 18 cents at $22.20 per MWh. NYMEX trade volumes were not immediately available, although trade was said to be very light while many players attended an industry conference in Vancouver today.

In the physical markets, day-head firm, peak power prices at PV were said to have traded at $53.00 per MWh after breaking above $100 yestersday, while those at COB were reported to have dropped $10.00 to $30.00-35.00 per MWh.
California and the interior section of the West was expected to have another day of scorching heat and record power demand Thursday.
Both Pacific Gas & Electric Co and Southern California Edison Co posted peak power demand records Wednesday due to soaring air-conditioning usage.
In the latest six to 10 day forecasts, the West was expected to experience a cooling trend, moderating toward more seasonal summer temperatures.

In generation news, the 220 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Four Corners generating complex in New Mexico was expected to resume operation early Friday after being shut Wednesday to repair a boiler tube leak.
The plant's two 750 MW units (4 and 5) and two 185 MW units (1 and 2) were operating at full output, Arizona Public Service Co said.

Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Wednesday operating transmission capacity on the AC portion of the Pacific Intertie system will hold at 3,450 megawatt (MW), although the operating limit of the AC part of the system was increased to 3,800 MW.
Electricity output from the 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 3 in Wintersburg, Ariz., continued to hold at 90 percent power early Thursday for repairs to a condensate pump.
The adjacent 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 2 was also operating at 90 percent of capacity as of early Thursday as the unit coasts down to a scheduled refueling outage September 6.
